unsupported_claims: LINE fails to scale on a typical single machine when the graph has millions of nodes and very many edges (accepts the false premise as its core conclusion)
LINE's training relies on alias tables requiring memory proportional to edges and nodes, which strains a single machine for hundreds of millions of edges

The answer characterizes LINE's runtime as prohibitive on one machine, contradicting the paper's claim of learning millions of vertices and billions of edges in a few hours on a typical single machine
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that LINE is efficient and can learn embeddings for networks with millions of vertices and billions of edges in a few hours on a typical single machine, so the answer's central claim that it fails in this setting is contradicted. The answer accepts the false premise and invents limitations (alias-table memory, prohibitive runtime) that the papers do not report.
